name: David Jolly
subject: I’m so proud to be your nominee for Florida Governor
body:
And new polling has JUST been released
| Friends,

Last week, Florida Democrats nominated me for Governor. I want to offer you my deepest thanks.

You showed up with grit and determination to transform this state and make Florida a better place to live and raise our families.

**Even better, a new poll just released, shows us up ONE point, 46-45%, over our Republican opponent, Byron Donalds.**

[Now, I need to ask: can you please split a contribution right now between our campaign and the Voter Protection Project to kick off the general election with the strongest start possible? ](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/126000?t=6&akid=28017%2E878179%2ENfQg18)

This poll is great news, but we need to act quickly to keep this race in play.

Byron Donalds has Donald Trump, the national Republican Party, and a wall of special interest money behind him. With friends like that, no wonder he’s raised more than $100 million.

And they're not going to stop. But neither are we.

We have hundreds of thousands of people who decided Florida is worth fighting for. That's what got us here, through the primary last week, and it's what will get us across the finish line.

My job is to go earn every vote in this state, in every corner of it, from Floridians who are done with the madness. And I need your support.

[So I’m asking: Will you split a contribution of $5, $10, or whatever you can right now to keep Florida in play as we kick off the general election? ](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/126000?t=7&akid=28017%2E878179%2ENfQg18) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between David Jolly and VPP will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $10 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/126001?t=8&akid=28017%2E878179%2ENfQg18)

This vignette is also from [_**TRAPPED**_](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/p9uxgn2z5eu9h2p435naqhpmw7p2qurhr480e/reh8hohm6v9vkwb2h6/dHJhcHBlZC52b3Rl)**** — a real-life cautionary tale about what can happen when elections become corrupted, institutions fail, and communities are slowly destroyed. The house you see is in Detroit, only miles from the Dearborn City Council meeting where Pastor Lorenzo spoke so passionately.
One video takes you to a Detroit address (one among thousands) documented as vacant across years, yet tied to an extraordinary number of voters. The other takes you just down the road, where Pastor Lorenzo repeatedly asked elected officials to renounce Sharia law. **Not one answered him.**
Why was he there? Because two weeks earlier there had been a violent confrontation in Dearborn at which activist Jake Lang, while publicly speaking about Jesus, was punched, chased and pelted with rocks before finding shelter in a police car. It feels dystopian. It feels like this cannot possibly be happening here. It is.
This has been building for years, right under our noses, but profound change rarely announces itself all at once.
I love the line from Hemingway’s _The Sun Also Rises_ , when a character describes bankruptcy as happening _“gradually and then suddenly.”_
I believe the bankruptcy we are witnessing in America is, at its root, a bankruptcy of courage — a failure of leadership, grit, conviction, and the willingness to endure discomfort and speak out when doing so comes at a cost.
**Courage is lost the same way — gradually, then suddenly.** A little silence here, a little retreat there, until suddenly we realize how much ground we have surrendered.
Too many of us have waited for someone else to go first. We have outsourced courage and then wondered why courageous voices seem so rare.
That is why the documentary _TRAPPED_ matters.
It is not simply a documentary about Detroit. **It is a warning.** We are seeing a glimpse of America’s future if we continue waiting for someone else to speak, someone else to serve, someone else to take the risk.
That has to change. We must engage while there is still time to do so — and for the 2026 midterms, that time is short.
Here is the hard truth: the practical window for election process reforms in this cycle has largely passed. We should continue pressing for comprehensive audits, stronger laws, transparency, and accountability, but we cannot recover months already lost. What’s done is done. We have to be smart about what comes next.
We are hearing from people across the country who are deeply concerned because they do not know what they can still do to bring integrity into their local elections.
**Do not confuse “we cannot fix everything” with “there is nothing we can do.”** There is meaningful work we can do right now:
1. **Make sure your family and friends**[**are registered to vote.**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/p9uxgn2z5eu9h2p435naqhpmw7p2qurhr480e/08hwh9h2lw0wnzslh5/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvcmVnaXN0cmF0aW9u) Ask them. Don’t assume.
2. **Check your own registration and voter records through our app**[**ScanCheckProtect.org**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/p9uxgn2z5eu9h2p435naqhpmw7p2qurhr480e/8ghqhohorpepwkhkh9/c2NhbmNoZWNrcHJvdGVjdC5vcmc=)**.** If something is inaccurate, report it. Individual records can still be corrected, and even when an issue cannot immediately be resolved, documenting and flagging it matters. Imagine the impact if millions of Americans simply checked and corrected their own records.
3. And **serve where you live.** Contact the party or candidate of your choice. Become an election worker or observer where permitted. Find your local election-integrity effort and offer to help. Our [**state Information page** ](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/p9uxgn2z5eu9h2p435naqhpmw7p2qurhr480e/08hwh9h2lw0wnzslh5/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvcmVnaXN0cmF0aW9u)has the resources and training to get you started, and the [**True the Vote Community app**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/p9uxgn2z5eu9h2p435naqhpmw7p2qurhr480e/vqh3hrhow323mmughl/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHBzLmFwcGxlLmNvbS91cy9hcHAvdHJ1ZS10aGUtdm90ZS1ub3cvaWQ2NzU2NjMyNTIz)can help you find others doing this work near you.

Young Americans can learn and serve. Older Americans can teach, mentor and support. Not everyone is called to do the same thing, but **every one of us has something to contribute — now.**
Meanwhile, as we prepare to release [_**TRAPPED**_**,**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/p9uxgn2z5eu9h2p435naqhpmw7p2qurhr480e/reh8hohm6v9vkwb2h6/dHJhcHBlZC52b3Rl) the pressure around its release is building. The documentary is not yet public and the negative press has already begun.
We will answer, point for point, but this is bigger than defending True the Vote, _TRAPPED_ , Detroit, or any single city or investigation. The deeper question is whether Americans still believe strongly enough in this country — and in one another — to stand up for it.
And as we stand, we must remember where our strength ultimately comes from.
**We cannot do this alone. We need God.**
Politics has limits. Institutions have limits. So do we. Faith is where we find the hope and the strength to persevere against all odds. It gives us courage when the path is unclear, endurance when the pressure is great, and the humility to understand that our responsibility is to faithfully do what we can and trust God with what we cannot control. Faith is not a retreat from the work. It is what allows us to continue the work without being consumed by fear or despair.
As a member of the True the Vote team wrote in our team thread early this morning, **“Your prayers are more powerful than a thousand political weapons.”**
I believe that.
So together, and in faith, we are asking you to engage now. Protect your vote. Help someone else protect theirs. Learn how your local elections work. Find somewhere useful to serve. Teach what you know. Learn what you don’t. Pray for wisdom and courage.
And when you see someone standing alone for the truth, **go stand beside them.**
Friend, this is the moment. **You were born for this time. Be brave.**
Keep the faith. Never quit. **Ephesians 6 FTW!**
Ever onward —
---
P.S. — One more thing I have to communicate in this email — [**we need your support.**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/p9uxgn2z5eu9h2p435naqhpmw7p2qurhr480e/l2hehmhlxv5vqei6h0/dHJ1ZXRoZXZvdGUub3JnL2RvbmF0ZQ==) I don’t like asking for money, but I would be less than honest if I pretended we could do this work without it. Supporting citizens on the ground, building the tools and training people need, finishing and releasing _TRAPPED_ , and standing our ground when the attacks come all require resources.
The truth is, **we are running on fumes. I wish it weren't the case, but it is.**
In the coming weeks, we will be launching a new recurring-giving campaign designed to help put this work on stronger footing for the battles ahead. I’ll have much more to share about that soon, so please stay tuned.
But our need today is immediate. We cannot wait for the next campaign to keep the work moving now.
If you believe this work matters, and you are able, [**please send support today.**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/p9uxgn2z5eu9h2p435naqhpmw7p2qurhr480e/l2hehmhlxv5vqei6h0/dHJ1ZXRoZXZvdGUub3JnL2RvbmF0ZQ==)
Whatever the amount, please know how deeply grateful we are — and how seriously we take the responsibility to put it to work.

[**Please Help Us If You Can**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/p9uxgn2z5eu9h2p435naqhpmw7p2qurhr480e/m2h7h5h340k025fmhq/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvZG9uYXRl)

### **Make Sure Our Emails Always Reach You**
UPDATE: We continue to get "Hellos" and they absolutely make our day. 😊 If you've followed the steps below, no need to do it again. If you missed it.... here's what this is all about. Sending email to our entire list has become increasingly difficult. Our detractors have made a practice of filing complaints about our weekly messages, and those complaints train the filters — which means frictionless delivery is now nearly impossible. And we expect it to get harder, not easier. **The most reliable fix is on your end: please whitelist our name.** It takes less than a minute, and it works in every email program, old or new. Here's how to do it:
1. Open your email program and find a message from True the Vote — check your Spam, Junk, or Promotions folder if you don't see one in your inbox.
2. If it's in Spam or Junk, click **Not Spam** (or **Not Junk**), then move the message to your inbox.
3. Open one of our emails and add the sender address — [**catherinee@truethevote.org**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/p9uxgn2z5eu9h2p435naqhpmw7p2qurhr480e/dpheh0hepwzwdncmh4/bWFpbHRvOmNhdGhlcmluZWVAdHJ1ZXRoZXZvdGUub3Jn)**** — to your contacts or address book. In most programs you can right-click the sender's name and choose **Add to Contacts.**
4. To seal the deal, reply to this email with a quick "hello" — even one word. Nothing signals "this sender is welcome" more strongly than a reply.

That's it. This same four-step habit works for True the Vote or any sender you don't want to miss — your bank, your doctor, your church. Thank you for taking a moment to keep our line open. We'll keep doing our part with our email provider, and together we'll stay connected. |

We need stamps for these postcards!

| |

| | Dear David, This week, our volunteers were unstoppable. They made thousands of phone calls and knocked on thousands of doors **because they believe in what we can accomplish when we work together.** [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/QTxJHyOqrL2QLUBFatzqKQ~~/AAUS1hA~/kxlocuAK4mM8M3heBzHptXDXiyt-6B-1C34ELLnC2ALNo72AAHenyegTjlsbGu4MJ0khv_MrQF6HIKGaHNDLhhv9xpg1DCnC2LB53lIIxTYmQ3vUWbIBbf8ibMZU2Kfesg6XBVZ-S3gFCuK2sstztaWwqTZM8sx2CVTkxw79bSTuPCQM7wt8Y80QPCVuGKJ3vuyQGoh2OJZd2zYc_Nrs3MST52zStqnVUCYGBrE6A6D3N6WVML2V1-n3cpiC3NZuRDYAh5i4psqmYcZ8ITSqNQ~~) The results in Michigan and Florida proved that direct, personal outreach like a volunteer at your door or a postcard in your mailbox can move the needle in a way that no television ad can. **That’s why we set an incredibly important goal: Raise $4,900 to purchase enough stamps to deliver those 35,000 handwritten postcards to our neighbors across the district.** Yes, 35,000 handwritten postcards. While most Americans don't get access to private briefings, inside information, or advance knowledge of government actions, members of Congress do. # [Proud to Fight for the Freedom to Create the Families We Choose!](https://bethfarnhamforcongress.com/2026/08/23/proud-to-fight-for-the-freedom-to-create-the-families-we-choose/?jetpack_skip_subscription_popup)

By **Elizabeth Farnham** on August 23, 2026
---
| **District Round-up 08.23.26**
---
Dear Neighbor, Thank you for reading my District Round-up. As your candidate for Pennsylvania’s 13th Congressional District, it is my honor and pleasure to deliver to you where I’ve been and what issues I’ve tackled in the past week. Criss-crossing the counties of Adams, Franklin, Fulton, Bedford, Cambria, Blair, Huntingdon, Mifflin, Juniata, Perry, Cumberland, and Somerset gives me great opportunities to meet with voters, hear what is on your hearts and minds, and the chance to voice my fight for Everyday Americans. If you would like to contribute to my campaign, please donate here:**[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/beth-farnham-for-congress-1](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=5c1e13a7bed4973960c4724d14338086b71acefd092316c1346501f71477ade8&blog_id=213069660&post_id=8738&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=84854051d495e0e3c5de42e2a5d99865&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL2JldGgtZmFybmhhbS1mb3ItY29uZ3Jlc3MtMQ=&email_id=044a6f035030d1210dc150a043dae1a7)**
---
| **Johnstown Pride**
---
| |
---
Many thanks to Johnstown Pride and Keystone Alliance Gay life Newsletter for hosting the Johnstown Pride festival and inviting me to speak on Saturday at 1st Summit Arena in Johnstown, Cambria County.
---
I enjoyed speaking with many voters who worry about their rights to vote, to create the family they choose, to continue to be married to the love of their life.
---
I let them know that I run this race to defend our agency over our own bodies, to create the families we choose, to love whom we love, and have the state fully recognize marriage of consenting adults.
---
They listened to me in the booth and on the stage and agreed to vote for me on November 3rd.
---
Many thanks to Campaign Manager Jack Stansbury for accompanying me to set up, tear down, and engage voters.
---
Together, we [#ChooseDemocracy](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=563ba312869f99725fb26850bf0f94fc6bf55ac24dba3a6d839f426c9e9d0ee8&blog_id=213069660&post_id=8738&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=1d5c5be2710309feff7f2c036f55208b&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=044a6f035030d1210dc150a043dae1a7) and equality!
---
| | |
---|---|---
| **Flock Flak**
---
| |
---
“Mom, Mom, it’s a Flock camera!”
---
As I entered the parking lot of a popular big box store, I looked over and noticed a thin pole whiz by. After parking, much to the embarrassment of my children, I approached the camera, trying to understand a little more about it.
---
Clearly, it was positioned on the store property. Moreover, it was aimed at the parking lot of the store.
---
Was this the government surveillance my children were trying to warn me about?
---
I took a picture and approached the store where plenty of other store cameras were aimed at me from the store perspective. Then, I entered the store, and asked for the manager.
---
After a little bit of time, and what seemed like some low-toned conversations over the phone, a manager approached and kindly answered my questions.
---
No, neither the police, nor the government owned it or any of the others on the property. These Flock cameras belonged to the store. After listening to their explanation, I understood that the cameras were really used to guard against theft and had been in place for a few years already.
---
I thanked the manager, bought what we needed, then headed home to do more research.
---
While I accept that store owners will film me on their property, the problem with Flock cameras in several areas is that the police departments and municipalities include budget lines, and therefore access, to them.
---
I don’t believe this was the case at the big box store or the municipality where I was, but I balk at the idea that the government would pay for them, even for the public areas, as they currently are.
---
For the uninitiated, Flock cameras, or scanners known as “automated license plate reader” or ALPRs, use exceptional technology to capture, retain, and filter/sort license plate numbers which can be shared across their vast network of 120,000 cameras and their servers.
---
If you’re a criminal, then ALPRs are some of your worst enemies, but if you’re an innocent person, ALPRs aren’t your friends either because that retention of information can be used by unscrupulous people to track down: ex-lovers, or people trying to obtain an abortion in a different state, or just cataloguing people’s patterns in everyday life.
---
For Americans who value privacy, this is an egregious overreach by The State, especially as no third party is involved in the oversight of ALPRs to prevent abuse of the information.
---
To resolve the first issue, Flock agreed to retain the information of innocent people for only 7 days, but they have various exceptions they can deploy to override that for longer, and since people have abused the data, I believe the ACLU’s recommendations of 48 hours and assigning a third party enforcer of standards of privacy, are far better.
---
In addition, I agree with Representative Thomas Massie (R-KY)’s proposal to block grants from the Department of Justice and Department of Homeland Security to the local municipalities and police departments for their purchase of ALPR’s.
---
However, I support private businesses/corporations that want to invest their own money in such devices. It has (almost) always been our choice to step onto private/corporate-owned property or not.
---
The public lands are a different matter and should be held to standards that are in keeping with our 4th Amendment Right which reads,”The right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers, and effects, against unreasonable searches and seizures, shall not be violated, and no Warrants shall issue, but upon probable cause, supported by Oath or affirmation, and particularly describing the place to be searched, and the persons or things to be seized.”
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and our Constitutional Rights!

After parking, much to the embarrassment of my children, I approached the camera, trying to understand a little more about it. Clearly, it was positioned on the store property. Moreover, it was aimed at the parking lot of the store. Was this the government surveillance my children were trying to warn me about? I took a picture and approached the store where plenty of other store cameras were aimed at me from the store perspective. Then, I entered the store, and asked for the manager. After a little bit of time, and what seemed like some low-toned conversations over the phone, a manager approached and kindly answered my questions. No, neither the police, nor the government owned it or any of the others on the property. These Flock cameras belonged to the store. After listening to their explanation, I understood that the cameras were really used to guard against theft and had been in place for a few years already. I thanked the manager, bought what we needed, then headed home to do more research. While I accept that store owners will film me on their property, the problem with Flock cameras in several areas is that the police departments and municipalities include budget lines, and therefore access, to them. I don’t believe this was the case at the big box store or the municipality where I was, but I balk at the idea that the government would pay for them, even for the public areas, as they currently are. For the uninitiated, Flock cameras, or scanners known as “automated license plate reader” or ALPRs, use exceptional technology to capture, retain, and filter/sort license plate numbers which can be shared across their vast network of 120,000 cameras and their servers. If you’re a criminal, then ALPRs are some of your worst enemies, but if you’re an innocent person, ALPRs aren’t your friends either because that retention of information can be used by unscrupulous people to track down: ex-lovers, or people trying to obtain an abortion in a different state, or just cataloguing people’s patterns in everyday life. For Americans who value privacy, this is an egregious overreach by The State, especially as no third party is involved in the oversight of ALPRs to prevent abuse of the information. To resolve the first issue, Flock agreed to retain the information of innocent people for only 7 days, but they have various exceptions they can deploy to override that for longer, and since people have abused the data, I believe the ACLU’s recommendations of 48 hours and assigning a third party enforcer of standards of privacy, are far better. In addition, I agree with Representative Thomas Massie (R-KY)’s proposal to block grants from the Department of Justice and Department of Homeland Security to the local municipalities and police departments for their purchase of ALPR’s. They use these models that are highly inaccurate to try to convince unsuspecting people that women and girls should suffer unwanted pregnancies. As if a fetus is simply a baby, but a smaller size . Since over 90% of abortions take place during the first 13 weeks, let’s compare and contrast their models to actual fetal pictures. Oh, look at that – COMPLETELY DIFFERENT! And if these prolife organizations are lying about what a fetus looks like at a particular age...WHAT ELSE ARE THEY LYING ABOUT? We already know that crisis pregnancy centers are not licensed healthcare centers, that the equipment is not inspected by the state government, that the workers are usually just church ladies in scrubs with a very fixed agenda. You don’t believe me? Feel free to consult the American College of Obstetrics and Gynecology about those facilities, or read the startling article about the Kentucky nurse who discovered expired disinfectant for the vaginal probes of the ultrasound. Don’t fall for the prolife claptrap. People aren’t going to adopt other people’s unwanted children. Take a look at the hundreds of children available at the Pennsylvania Department of Human Health services. Meanwhile, millions of other children go hungry in America alone which is why No Kid Hungry charity and others like it exist. It helps then to understand that 60% of people who seek abortion identify as MOTHERS. They know what it is to sustain a pregnancy, give birth, then raise a child. They’re saying, “I can’t do this.” And if they can’t, you won’t. You won’t provide prenatal visits for them to go to, prenatal vitamins for them to take, childcare and/or time off of work as needed. So don’t fool yourself. But do agree with the right of a person to make their own decisions about their own bodies. And please vote for me, Beth Farnham, on November 3rd. **" Texas Lacks Statewide Record of Water Use, Local Tax Breaks for Data Centers"** via [The Texan](https://substack.com/redirect/7a19818a-a7ae-47c4-b879-b73988b59efe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Isaiah Mitchell** - The Texas Legislature is preparing to address data center development using information reported by the developers themselves, according to state officials.

During a lengthy hearing in the Texas Capitol on Wednesday, several public officials told the State Affairs Committee of the Texas House that agencies do not comprehensively track data centers ' water usage or the local tax breaks they receive. The state instead relies on survey responses.

The committee heard from **Pablo Vegas** , CEO of the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT), and **Thomas Gleeson** , chairman of the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUC), the two agencies responsible for managing Texas' electrical infrastructure. Earlier this month, Gov. **Greg Abbott** asked these agencies to audit all data center projects in the process of connecting to the Texas power grid, specifying that the PUC and ERCOT must learn which projects benefit from state and local tax breaks.

"Are either the PUC or ERCOT set up to undertake that type of review of local tax incentives or abatements, or anything on the state level, for that matter?" state Rep. **Chris Turner** (D-Arlington) asked Pablo Vegas and Thomas Gleeson. Vegas told Turner that they'll ask for this information through a survey. During a tense exchange with state Rep. **Richard Pe ña Raymond** (D-Laredo), officials representing the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) and the Texas Water Development Board (TWDB) also told the lawmaker that their agencies don't maintain a statewide record of data centers' water usage, which can vary considerably from one project to another. _([THE TEXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/7a19818a-a7ae-47c4-b879-b73988b59efe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Paxton Bars More Than 110 Cities From Raising Taxes Over Audit Failures"** via [Texas Scorecard](https://substack.com/redirect/0823cd25-554e-4db9-8d1e-69819e567c80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Sydnie Henry** - Attorney General**Ken Paxton** has notified more than 110 additional Texas cities that they may not raise their property tax rates above the no-new-revenue rate after his office found they failed to meet state financial audit and transparency requirements.

The latest notices expand Paxton's enforcement effort under Senate Bill 1851, a 2025 law that limits a noncompliant municipality's authority to raise ad valorem taxes. In May, the attorney general notified more than 130 cities of the same restriction after reviewing records from more than 1,000 municipalities statewide.

"I am continuing to fight to stop cities from unlawfully raising taxes on hardworking Texans," Paxton said. "My office has been investigating cities across Texas. Now, over 110 new cities have been notified that they must not raise property taxes in violation of state law. I will continue to make sure that taxpayers are protected from unlawful tax increases."

SB 1851 requires a municipality to have its records and accounts audited annually and to prepare an annual financial statement based on that audit. Cities must also file the financial statement and the auditor's opinion with the municipal secretary or clerk within 180 days of the end of the city's fiscal year. _([Texas Scorecard](https://substack.com/redirect/0823cd25-554e-4db9-8d1e-69819e567c80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Texas lawmakers turn against the massive power lines they ordered"** via [San Antonio Express-News](https://substack.com/redirect/579b7295-fcd1-45e5-9f88-44c4e8ab3163?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)' **Kelsey Brown** - Texas lawmakers are telling the Public Utility Commission to hold up on building massive power lines to West Texas, just two years after ordering the construction to meet a surge in demand driven by the electrification of the oil and gas industry and data centers. The about-face comes after a 15-hour public hearing last month illuminated the issues faced by landowners in the planning process for development of the state's largest-ever transmission lines.

At a meeting, the state utility regulator took no action to halt the development set to begin with a $1.4 billion line that could cut through 14 counties in the Hill Country to transport power from San Antonio to West Texas. A House committee is to conduct a hearing and the PUC could review one of the planned lines. The series of lines is being planned under the $33 billion Permian Basin Reliability Plan, which would add 765-kilovolt transmission lines throughout the state.

Sen. **Charles Schwertner** , chair of the Senate Committee on Business and Commerce, said last month's hearing revealed "significant concerns" with the process, lack of proper notice from utilities, shortened timelines for utility commission proceedings and due process at the State Office of Administrative Hearings. He called on the PUC to deny the existing Certificate of Convenience and Necessity applications, which utilities file to build a new transmission line. _([SAEN](https://substack.com/redirect/579b7295-fcd1-45e5-9f88-44c4e8ab3163?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Exclusive: HISD touted gains. Ratings leaned on courses Texas deemed ineffective"** via [Houston Chronicle](https://substack.com/redirect/aa324083-5d76-4ee1-95dc-915fd61fe40a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Caroline Ghisolfi** - Two years into Houston ISD's state takeover, state-appointed Superintendent**Mike Miles** touted a major achievement: state ratings showed there were no more F-rated schools in the district.

Some of that jump, however, had little to do with Miles' sweeping reforms or gains in student test scores. One key factor was HISD's use of a new, rapidly expanding option in Texas' accountability system: college-prep courses.

These are not typical courses that can earn students college credit, such as Advanced Placement or dual credit. These are courses, often taken online, that help students catch up on English and math so they don't have to take remedial classes in college. In the state's accountability system, schools that enroll students in college-prep courses can earn credit for producing college-ready graduates, which in turn boosts their A-F ratings.

Exclusive data from the Texas Education Agency obtained by the Houston Chronicle shows that without students completing those courses, every high school in Miles' reform model would have dropped by at least one letter grade in 2025. The district would have had five D-rated and two F-rated high schools - undercutting Miles' claim of no F-rated campuses. _([HOU CHRON](https://substack.com/redirect/aa324083-5d76-4ee1-95dc-915fd61fe40a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Texas cities eye property tax hikes, spending cuts amid yawning budget gaps"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/3bc6c169-357a-41bd-9a69-2e475c4c61b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s**Joshua Fechter** - Texas cities have floated unusual proposals to slash their spending as they face yawning budget gaps, from laying off employees and charging non-residents higher zoo ticket prices, to asking voters to reconsider public funding to a new arena for the San Antonio Spurs.

These desperate maneuvers -- some of which have not come to fruition -- underscore how inflation, a slower economy and moves by state lawmakers have put Texas' biggest cities in a tightening financial noose that will take big moves to get out of.

"This is going to be our new normal going forward," Dallas City Manager **Kimberly Bizor Tolbert** said Tuesday during a briefing on the city's upcoming budget.

In Dallas, the budget gap is $51 million. In Fort Worth, it's $94 million. In San Antonio, the city faces a $158 million deficit over the next two years. Austin faces a structural deficit that could grow past $100 million by the start of the next decade. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/3bc6c169-357a-41bd-9a69-2e475c4c61b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Harris County Proposed $3.1 Billion Budget Proposal Will Require Property Tax Hike"** via [The Texan](https://substack.com/redirect/e521ff8c-27cb-4776-aad5-f4f7de1fddf6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Holly Hansen** - Harris County property owners may pay higher tax bills next year to cover a proposed $3.1 billion budget and bridge a projected $181 million shortfall.

Management and Budget Executive Director **Daniel Ramos** presented the Fiscal Year 2027 proposal to the Harris County Commissioners Court on Monday, with a plan to cover the shortfall with cost savings, land sales, and other new revenues -- and by adopting the Voter-Approval Rate (VAR), the maximum rate increase allowed under Texas law without voter approval.

Should commissioners approve the VAR next month, the overall property tax rate -- which includes the Harris County Flood Control District, the Harris Health hospital district, the Port of Houston, and the county's general fund -- will increase from $0.6241 to about $0.68 per $100 of appraised value.

Commissioners **Adrian Garcia** (D-Pct. 2) and **Lesley Briones** (D-Pct. 4) blamed the county's budget woes on unfunded mandates from the state, Texas lawmakers' refusal to expand Medicaid, and federal changes to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program and the Affordable Care Act. _([THE TEXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/e521ff8c-27cb-4776-aad5-f4f7de1fddf6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Can Austin break the costly cycle of homelessness, jail and crisis? A new program aims to do that."** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/753cdd29-4170-439b-9d43-73af78f11b77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - About six months behind bars, **Marcus Martin** walked out of the Travis County Correctional Complex in Southeast Austin, a broad smile stretched across his face. He's been incarcerated before, but he believes this time is different.

Outside the facility, several people awaited his release in their vehicles, blasting the air conditioning, while another went inside to greet Martin, made sure he had all of his belongings and walked him through what came next. The team waiting for him were not social workers, case managers or family, but sworn Austin Police Department officers assigned to a new program called No Wrong Door, a cross-agency effort aimed at helping people experiencing homelessness with complex mental health disorders who have frequent interactions with law enforcement and public health systems.

Martin is one of roughly 950 people local officials identify as the county's highest "utilizers," residents whose repeated arrests, emergency room visits, psychiatric crises and criminal trespasses cost an estimated $137 million in public resources each year while often leaving the underlying problems untreated. Austin leaders believe No Wrong Door, could change that by coordinating police, hospitals, homeless service providers and other agencies around people who have proven hardest for existing systems to reach.

For Martin, a series of life events and a bad breakup led to him becoming homeless for several years. Drug use kept him there and away from his family. "With me going down the rabbit hole I was going down, it wasn't productive or beneficial for me to be around them," he said. "I was being selfish, to be honest with you, and chose drugs over my own safety." That rabbit hole led to frequent interactions with local law enforcement and, eventually, a jail sentence. It also led to Martin being identified as a candidate for No Wrong Door while behind bars. Officers in the program met with him while he was incarcerated to determine what support he would need upon release to stay healthy and out of jail. For Martin, that meant checking in at an Integral Care clinic to continue receiving mental health treatment. Martin said "I'm ready to grow," he said. "I think it's gonna be a beautiful thing." _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/753cdd29-4170-439b-9d43-73af78f11b77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Bexar County health department at risk as ARPA money runs out"** via [San Antonio Report](https://substack.com/redirect/f2a62fe9-37cd-44ac-97fc-9e394fc65be2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Josh Archote** - Two years into the COVID-19 pandemic, Bexar County spent millions in federal pandemic relief dollars on public health programs -- with the goal of getting more involved in preventative health, preparing for future pandemics and addressing longstanding health inequities.

Now, the funds are expiring at the same time the county budget is being squeezed, raising uncertainty about the future of the county's public health department, particularly its newly created Preventative Health Division.

Created in 2022, the division now operates a $10 million annual budget, including 28 staff positions and programs supporting victims of domestic violence, elder abuse and other public health initiatives, according to a county budget document. Given the budget picture, some county commissioners are suggesting combining county efforts with University Health's Public Health Division, which was also established that year with the help of temporary American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding.

Former Bexar County Judge **Nelson Wolff** , who championed the project, said in an interview that he wasn't sure if the county's preventative health campaigns had been effective -- or what the division had done since he left office. "I don't know whether they've done any good with it or not," he said. "Maybe just another bureaucratic department, as far as I know, and if that's true, then there's no need to have it. But if they have done some good things and they can be transferred over to University Hospital, then that ought to be done." _([SA REPORT](https://substack.com/redirect/f2a62fe9-37cd-44ac-97fc-9e394fc65be2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

TOP NEWS " Data centers in Texas prove a key topic months away from midterm elections" via ' Steven Rosenbaum - As the public backlash to data center construction continues in both suburban and rural parts of Texas, Gov. Greg Abbott is touting that major tech companies like Google, Amazon and Microsoft are signing on to guidelines he has implemented to "ensure data center development does not come at the expense of Texas families or communities". The guidelines include undergoing audits from ERCOT and the Public Utility Commission of Texas over electricity use, water consumption, noise and light pollution and other impacts on nearby property owners. Abbott says data center projects that do not comply with the audits will not be approved. A recent poll by Texas Public Opinion Research shows more than 75 percent of Texans support requiring large AI data centers to disclose water consumption, avoid tapping overused aquifers, fund conservation projects, fund their own grid upgrades, and not pass the costs onto other electricity ratepayers. () " Texas Lacks Statewide Record of Water Use, Local Tax Breaks for Data Centers" via Isaiah Mitchell - The Texas Legislature is preparing to address data center development using information reported by the developers themselves, according to state officials. During a lengthy hearing in the Texas Capitol on Wednesday, several public officials told the State Affairs Committee of the Texas House that agencies do not comprehensively track data centers ' water usage or the local tax breaks they receive. The state instead relies on survey responses. The committee heard from Pablo Vegas , CEO of the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT), and Thomas Gleeson , chairman of the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUC), the two agencies responsible for managing Texas' electrical infrastructure. Earlier this month, Gov. Greg Abbott asked these agencies to audit all data center projects in the process of connecting to the Texas power grid, specifying that the PUC and ERCOT must learn which projects benefit from state and local tax breaks. "Are either the PUC or ERCOT set up to undertake that type of review of local tax incentives or abatements, or anything on the state level, for that matter?" state Rep. Chris Turner (D-Arlington) asked Pablo Vegas and Thomas Gleeson. Vegas told Turner that they'll ask for this information through a survey. During a tense exchange with state Rep. Richard Pe ña Raymond (D-Laredo), officials representing the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) and the Texas Water Development Board (TWDB) also told the lawmaker that their agencies don't maintain a statewide record of data centers' water usage, which can vary considerably from one project to another. () " Texas's Data Center Dominance At Risk" via Hugh Cameron - Texas is leading the way when it comes to data center development in the U.S., but local opposition and now official moratoriums may be threatening what developers see as the potential benefits from the state's central role in the AI boom. Data center expansion has emerged as a national flashpoint, with officials and companies themselves touting the economic value and strategic importance of securing America's edge in the AI race, though surveys continue to chart widespread disapproval from voters across the country. A Reuters/Ipsos poll from June found that 57 percent would oppose a data center being built in their community, a figure that reached 71 percent in an earlier survey from Gallup. In an interview with Punchbowl News in early August, President Donald Trump called data centers "tremendously important" while acknowledging Americans' unease about the ongoing buildout. "Whoever wins AI just wins. It's that big. It's bigger than the internet by many times. It's gonna be bigger than anybody ever thought possible. Not even imaginable how big," the president said. "I saw Texas the other day sort of is against data centers. I think it's a mistake." In a recent note, Torsten Slok , chief economist at Apollo Global Management, described America's "data center boom" as "a Texas Story." he cited research from the market intelligence platform Cleanview, which found that Texas--while second to Virginia in current operating capacity--now accounts for more planned capacity by megawatts (94,656 MW) than the next three states combined. CyrusOne, a company which currently boasts 15 data centers in Texas, told Newsweek. "Maintaining that leadership will help sustain job creation, workforce development, local tax revenue and the infrastructure needed to support the state's continued economic growth." Ray Perryman , president and CEO of The Perryman Group, an economic research and analysis firm based in Waco, Texas, likewise described them as a "major source of investment throughout Texas," but one which community opposition could complicate. () " Judge upholds temporary halt on border wall construction along wildlife refuge" via Sandra Sanchez - A federal judge is keeping in place a temporary order preventing border wall construction at Santa Ana National Wildlife Refuge in Alamo, Texas, at least for a couple weeks. During a preliminary hearing on Monday, U.S. Magistrate Judge Juan Alanis, of the U.S. District Court of the Southern District of Texas in McAllen continued the temporary restraining order, which had stopped border wall construction along the refuge. He also set another hearing for Aug. 26 in the civil case. The Hidalgo County Irrigation District filed a lawsuit against Spencer Construction LLC, and Royal Concrete Products LLC, claiming border wall construction at Santa Ana National Wildlife that began in late July was "interfering and altering the property, canals and related irrigation infrastructure... without Plaintiff's consent," according to the lawsuit obtained by Border Report. The case was originally filed in state District Court but was bumped to federal court last week after the federal government joined as a third party saying it oversees Spencer Construction and all border wall related construction on the Southwest border. After the quick, 10-minute hearing on Monday, Ruben Pe ña, the lawyer representing Spencer Construction, told Border Report that the contractor used safeguards to prevent any damage to the canal when it began building the border wall in late July. () " Texas may soon have more people than California -- here's why" via Joel Kotkin - More than a half century ago California passed New York to become America's most populous state. It was not only first in population, but an industrial, agricultural, and technology behemoth that also provided most of the nation's entertainment. Today that primacy is threatened as never before, most powerfully by Texas, whose pro-business policies, low taxes and growing technical skill are propelling its economy. By 2050, for example, Texas is now slated to pass California in population, driven both by both immigration and domestic migration. Its economy is growing far faster, and it is now the headquarters of many former Californian companies. This year, for the first time, Texas passed California and New York as a headquarters for the nation's largest companies. Even the establishmentarian Economist recently proclaimed the Lone Star State is "America Inc.'s new centre of gravity." What should concern us are the reasons for this shift. After all, people don't move to Texas for better weather or scenery. Or for reasonable policies on issues like abortion. () " San Antonio City Council rejects public vote on $489M Spurs arena contribution" via Andrea Drusch - San Antonio City Council rejected calls to hold a public vote on its $489 million Spurs arena contribution on Monday, voting down a proposal to put it on the Nov. 3 midterm ballot. The move means that last November's election approving $311 million in Bexar County venue tax dollars for the arena, known as Proposition B, could be both the first and only time voters are asked about a public investment that totals more than $800 million. Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones called Monday's meeting knowing she likely lacked the support from colleagues to get a city vote on the ballot. Now that the council is facing a ballooning budget deficit, Jones said that investment of this scale deserved its own public hearing. The majority of her colleagues disagreed, saying it was bad for business to invite the public to weigh in on major spending decisions that don't legally require it. "We should be very careful about establishing a precedent that every significant revenue bond decision requires another election simply because the dollar amount is large," said Councilwoman Misty Spears , one of the nonpartisan panel's two most conservative members. () " Texas leads nation in restaurant closures" via -- Restaurant doors open every day across Texas, but for some owners, keeping those doors open has become an increasingly difficult challenge. A midyear report from RestaurantData shows 1,039 restaurant closures across Texas during the first half of 2026, the highest number of closures in the nation. At Renny's Bar and Grill in Dallas, owner Mark Maguire is a familiar presence, laughing with customers, checking in on tables and making sure guests feel at home. () " Taylor Sheridan shares update on 'Yellowstone' spinoff about Four Sixes Ranch" via Brayden Garcia - Taylor Sheridan has many irons in the fire, but there's one he's quenching into a bucket of water. More than five years ago, in February 2021, Paramount announced a new scripted series about the historic Four Sixes Ranch. The show, which had a working title of "6666," was announced as part of Taylor Sheridan's new slate of Paramount+ programming along with projects like "1883," "Landman" and "Mayor of Kingstown." It was apt timing to reveal the show, since "Yellowstone" viewers would soon see Jimmy (Jefferson White) be sent to the Guthrie, Texas, ranch in season 4, which premiered that November. The show announcement also came about a year before Taylor Sheridan and a group of investors purchased the ranch for more than $300 million in early 2022. On Dale Brisby 's "Rodeo Time," Taylor Sheridan detailed the latest on "6666." "There's never going to be one," Taylor Sheridan said. "I would never fictionalize that ranch." Taylor Sheridan continued that if he was to make a show about the ranch, he would have to trivialize and fictionalize a place where real people work and raise their families. () 2026 " Democratic Lt. Gov. candidate Vikki Goodwin challenges Republican Dan Patrick to debate" via '-- The Democratic candidate for lieutenant governor challenged three-term incumbent Republican Dan Patrick to a set of debates before the November election. Austin State Rep. Vikki Goodwin issued her challenge on Spectrum News' Capital Tonight. "What I would really like is a debate. I'd like to have three debates with Dan Patrick to really get the issues out there for the voters," she said. "I think voters deserve to have the candidates side by side, talking about the issues of the day." The Republican incumbent is heavily favored in the race, given the GOP's three decades of domination in state politics and his massive campaign war chest. Dan Patrick had $35 million in cash on hand in his last financial report covering the first six months of the year. () " Dallas group hits $45 million fundraising goal for Trump's GOP convention" via Kramon - The private group seeking support for President Donald Trump 's Republican convention in Dallas says it raised $45 million to help stage the two-day event next month. The Dallas 2026 Host Committee said contributions came from individuals and companies in Dallas, across Texas and nationwide. Like similar committees, it did not name donors or say how much each group gave. Ray Washburne , a developer and committee co-chair, said the group had "met its fundraising goals" and looked forward to "celebrating everything Dallas" at the GOP gathering Sept. 9-10 at American Airlines Center . "Donors were excited to support this historic event coming to Dallas since it is another way to showcase a vibrant downtown, our expertise in hosting large, high-profile events and our Texas hospitality," he told The Dallas Morning News. Andrew Cates , a San Antonio-based attorney who specializes in legislative and campaign law, said "If there's one thing that I know is that if the Republicans need to raise $30 million to $40 million, they can do it," () " Texas counties sue feds for trying to tie election security policies to anti-terrorism funding" via Ayden Runnels - El Paso County and Harris County on Monday sued the Department of Homeland Security alongside communities in Tennessee and Ohio over new requirements for federal grants that they argue undermine election security and public safety. In June, the Federal Emergency Management Agency announced it would withhold 20% of DHS' Homeland Security Grant Program funds unless grantees complied with five requirements that would shift how local officials conduct their elections. The new requirements include a mandatory transition from voting machines that accept QR and bar codes to ones that take paper ballots, conducting manual ballot audits and running voter registration through DHS' Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements system, better known as the SAVE system. The SAVE system has repeatedly been flagged for misidentifying voters as noncitizens, however the Trump administration has nevertheless pushed for its use amid false claims that millions of noncitizens are registered to vote. In late July, Texas' Secretary of State's Office directed county officials to reinstate some of the 2,724 registered voters who were flagged as potential noncitizens by the SAVE system. "Local election offices already face some of the toughest oversight and requirements designed to keep their operations safe and secure," Christina Sanchez said in a statement. "Imposing additional requirements is both costly and burdensome, while our law enforcement agencies rely on this funding to purchase critical equipment that helps protect and save lives." () " Elon Musk Is Expected to Point His Money Machine at Texas Politics" via Hugo Lowell - Elon Musk is expected to spend big to boost Republicans in the midterms this November, according to Trump officials briefed on the matter. The precise amount could change, but the officials expect Elon Musk to spend around $100 million to $200 million with a focus on voter turnout in key races, including Texas, where the fate of Republican nominee Ken Paxton could determine which party controls the US Senate. The planned cash injection--or any in-kind contribution relating to voter turnout--would be a boon for Ken Paxton, who has been vastly outraised in contributions. According to the latest FEC filings, James Talarico had raised roughly $69 million compared to Ken Paxton's $9 million. While an endorsement from President Donald Trump carried him to victory, Ken Paxton lagged behind in contributions throughout a bruising primary against Senator John Cornyn that resurfaced past scandals , and has fared little better since becoming the nominee. () " Senate hopeful Talarico touts his faith. Texas Republicans call it blasphemy." via Choi - State Rep. James Talarico is changing the script, leaning into his background in a progressive Presbyterian seminary. It's a playbook that has helped propel his political career. Before he was the Democrats' hope to flip a Republican Senate seat in Texas, the state lawmaker often invoked the Bible to justify progressive policy positions in the Texas Capitol. Past floor speeches and sermons on abortion, gender equity and religious pluralism helped give him the online platform that launched his Senate run. He is now making his faith a central part of his Senate campaign, telling voters "it's time to start flipping tables" and take back faith from the religious right -- a reference to the biblical story of Jesus flipping over tables in the Temple of Jerusalem to purge merchants profiting off a house of worship. James Talarico boils down his core message to two commandments from the Bible: Love God and love your neighbor. His allies say Talarico's approach could help win over faith-based voters in the Bible Belt's largest state. But Talarico's past remarks regarding the Bible have infuriated some evangelical voters, and attacking Talarico's comments is now a regular part of his Republican opponent's stump speech. "First of all, he said God is nonbinary. He also said, 'I'm a Christian, but I hate Christianity.' How many Christians do you know have said that?" Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton recently told an audience of supporters in North Texas. "I've never met one." Talarico, 37, and Paxton, a 63-year-old staunch evangelical Trump ally, are engaged in a competitive general election race that could be pivotal in Democrats' attempt to retake control of the Senate. () " Dallas activists seek nationwide turnout for protests at Trump's GOP convention" via ' Mar ia Ramos Pacheco and Chase Rogers - Historian Michael Phillips spoke Friday about the political history of Dallas and the protests at Dallas' 1984 Republican National Convention. A new generation of activists is preparing a series of protests when President Donald Trump arrives next month in Dallas for a national rally, 42 years after demonstrators targeted the city's last Republican national convention. The Dallas Against the Trump Agenda coalition is seeking city permits, lining up legal support, organizing safety training and even arranging sign-making sessions ahead of the Sept. 9-10 convention at the American Airlines Center. Jo Hargis of the DFW Anti-War Committee said the coalition is inviting organizations nationwide to participate and is ready to work with others opposed to the Trump administration. "People are welcome from all around the country to join in this protest," Hargis said. () STATE GOVERNMENT " Paxton Bars More Than 110 Cities From Raising Taxes Over Audit Failures" via Sydnie Henry - Attorney GeneralKen Paxton has notified more than 110 additional Texas cities that they may not raise their property tax rates above the no-new-revenue rate after his office found they failed to meet state financial audit and transparency requirements. The latest notices expand Paxton's enforcement effort under Senate Bill 1851, a 2025 law that limits a noncompliant municipality's authority to raise ad valorem taxes. In May, the attorney general notified more than 130 cities of the same restriction after reviewing records from more than 1,000 municipalities statewide. "I am continuing to fight to stop cities from unlawfully raising taxes on hardworking Texans," Paxton said. "My office has been investigating cities across Texas. Now, over 110 new cities have been notified that they must not raise property taxes in violation of state law. I will continue to make sure that taxpayers are protected from unlawful tax increases." SB 1851 requires a municipality to have its records and accounts audited annually and to prepare an annual financial statement based on that audit. Cities must also file the financial statement and the auditor's opinion with the municipal secretary or clerk within 180 days of the end of the city's fiscal year. () " Texas Ten Commandments lawsuits could advance to U.S. Supreme Court" via ' Sophia Veneziano - Two lawsuits challenging a Texas law that requires public schools to post donated copies of the Ten Commandments in every classroom may advance to the U.S. Supreme Court. More than 20 Texas families on Monday requested that the nation's highest court hear their challenges to Senate Bill 10, which lawmakers passed in 2025. The law has drawn several legal challenges across the state since it went into effect. The families asked the Supreme Court to review lower court decisions in two separate cases. One of the lawsuits was filed by San Antonio Rabbi Mara Nathan against the Alamo Heights Independent School District, and the other was filed by Comal ISD parent Roxanne Cribbs Ringer against her district. () " Minnesota sues to force Greg Abbott to extradite ICE agent in shooting case" via Wermund - The state of Minnesota is asking a federal judge to force Gov. Greg Abbott to authorize the extradition of a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent accused of shooting a Minneapolis man earlier this year. The lawsuit, filed Tuesday, says the Republican governor has delayed the extradition of the ICE officer, Christian J. Castro , 52, for months -- to the point that Castro could soon be eligible for release under Texas law, which sets a 90-day limit on detention of fugitives awaiting extradition. Abbott said Tuesday that he will not respond to Minnesota's request "at all" until officials "acknowledge their fault" in a series of fraud cases involving government programs. "I don't trust Tim Walz on anything, let alone something like this," Abbott said of the Minnesota governor. () " Texas Gov. Greg Abbott calls for a ban on H-1B visas for public school employees" via Eleanor Dearman - Texas Gov. Greg Abbott on Tuesday called for legislation banning H-1B visas for public school employees. Abbott made the remarks during a news conference in Austin focused on stopping "foreign influence" in K-12 schools. One step towards that goal is barring the federal temporary work visas that are reserved for high-skilled immigrant workers, the governor said. The legislative proposal follows Abbott's January directive to state agencies and public universities and colleges to halt new H-1B visas. "Exactly zero Texas public school employees should be here on H-1B visas," Abbott said. Additionally, lawmakers should pass legislation that prohibits public schools from taking gifts, money or property from foreign sources, Abbott said. He said schools should also be barred from "entering into partnerships or financial agreements with a foreign source." The proposals are Abbott's latest policy announcements related to education, as he bids against state Rep. Gina Hinojosa , an Austin Democrat, for governor in the Nov. 3 general election. () " Dan Patrick: "We're coming for the books" in school libraries" via Alejandro Serrano - Lt. Gov.Dan Patrick on Wednesday vowed to pass legislation punishing public schools that do not remove graphic books from their shelves by knocking them down a notch in the state's annual school performance ratings, which the state uses to seize control of underperforming districts. Flanked by easels displaying printed covers of books he found obscene, the lieutenant governor said school boards and administrators have not been following a 2025 law aimed at weeding out lewd books from the shelves in Texas' more than 9,000 campuses attended by some 5.5 million schoolchildren. "It's the law and we expect you to follow the law. So we're coming for the books," Patrick said during a news conference at the Texas Capitol. "We ask that you do it on your own and remove these books." Patrick noted at his press conference, however, that more than 90% of parents and grandparents would not want their kids seeing the books he was highlighting, some of which depicted masturbation and graphic images of genitalia. Dan Patrick is up for reelection and will face state Rep. Vikki Goodwin in November. () " Failing AISD campuses reach Texas threshold for state intervention" via Austin Current's Andrea Ball - Austin school district leaders are determined to turn around the two middle schools that triggered mandatory state intervention. Whether they get the chance may no longer be up to them. Burnet and Webb middle schools received their fifth consecutive F ratings from the Texas Education Agency, triggering a state law that requires the agency to intervene. What that intervention ultimately looks like remains unclear. Under the new statewide ratings released Friday, it is the only Texas district to trigger a potential state takeover. But the ratings also left the district with an argument that it is making progress. The district overall earned a B grade, up from a C last year, said Superintendent Matias Segura. And Dobie Middle School, which was teetering on its fifth failing score, earned a D this year. Matias Segura says he won't speculate on TEA's next move and, as of Wednesday, had not spoken to the agency about the pending state intervention. Instead, he said, educators remain focused on improving all the schools, including Webb, Burnet and Dobie. "I've spent time at those three schools last week, even prior to that," Segura said. "We have two new leaders at those schools. The system is now better positioned to move the outcomes based on what we went through last year." () " Former Texas Lottery chief heads to court. Here's how the agency's troubles unfolded" via Lucio Vasquez |The Texas Newsroom - More than three years after a group of gamblers spent millions of dollars buying nearly every possible combination for a Texas lottery drawing, the fallout is moving into a new phase: criminal court. Gary Grief , the former longtime executive director of the Texas Lottery Commission, faces a first-degree felony charge of abuse of official capacity over the April 2023 Lotto Texas drawing. The commission itself -- an agency that no longer exists -- has also been indicted on the same charge. The cases stem from a Texas Rangers investigation into a $95 million jackpot that set off years of scrutiny over how the state lottery was run, its relationship with private lottery businesses and the commission's role in facilitating the massive ticket purchase. () #TXLEGE " Texas lawmakers turn against the massive power lines they ordered" via ' Kelsey Brown - Texas lawmakers are telling the Public Utility Commission to hold up on building massive power lines to West Texas, just two years after ordering the construction to meet a surge in demand driven by the electrification of the oil and gas industry and data centers. The about-face comes after a 15-hour public hearing last month illuminated the issues faced by landowners in the planning process for development of the state's largest-ever transmission lines. At a meeting, the state utility regulator took no action to halt the development set to begin with a $1.4 billion line that could cut through 14 counties in the Hill Country to transport power from San Antonio to West Texas. A House committee is to conduct a hearing and the PUC could review one of the planned lines. The series of lines is being planned under the $33 billion Permian Basin Reliability Plan, which would add 765-kilovolt transmission lines throughout the state. Sen. Charles Schwertner , chair of the Senate Committee on Business and Commerce, said last month's hearing revealed "significant concerns" with the process, lack of proper notice from utilities, shortened timelines for utility commission proceedings and due process at the State Office of Administrative Hearings. He called on the PUC to deny the existing Certificate of Convenience and Necessity applications, which utilities file to build a new transmission line. () LOCAL GOVERNMENT " Exclusive: HISD touted gains. Ratings leaned on courses Texas deemed ineffective" via Caroline Ghisolfi - Two years into Houston ISD's state takeover, state-appointed SuperintendentMike Miles touted a major achievement: state ratings showed there were no more F-rated schools in the district. Some of that jump, however, had little to do with Miles' sweeping reforms or gains in student test scores. One key factor was HISD's use of a new, rapidly expanding option in Texas' accountability system: college-prep courses. These are not typical courses that can earn students college credit, such as Advanced Placement or dual credit. These are courses, often taken online, that help students catch up on English and math so they don't have to take remedial classes in college. In the state's accountability system, schools that enroll students in college-prep courses can earn credit for producing college-ready graduates, which in turn boosts their A-F ratings. Exclusive data from the Texas Education Agency obtained by the Houston Chronicle shows that without students completing those courses, every high school in Miles' reform model would have dropped by at least one letter grade in 2025. The district would have had five D-rated and two F-rated high schools - undercutting Miles' claim of no F-rated campuses. () " Texas cities eye property tax hikes, spending cuts amid yawning budget gaps" via Fechter - Texas cities have floated unusual proposals to slash their spending as they face yawning budget gaps, from laying off employees and charging non-residents higher zoo ticket prices, to asking voters to reconsider public funding to a new arena for the San Antonio Spurs. These desperate maneuvers -- some of which have not come to fruition -- underscore how inflation, a slower economy and moves by state lawmakers have put Texas' biggest cities in a tightening financial noose that will take big moves to get out of. "This is going to be our new normal going forward," Dallas City Manager Kimberly Bizor Tolbert said Tuesday during a briefing on the city's upcoming budget. In Dallas, the budget gap is $51 million. In Fort Worth, it's $94 million. In San Antonio, the city faces a $158 million deficit over the next two years. Austin faces a structural deficit that could grow past $100 million by the start of the next decade. () " Harris County Proposed $3.1 Billion Budget Proposal Will Require Property Tax Hike" via Holly Hansen - Harris County property owners may pay higher tax bills next year to cover a proposed $3.1 billion budget and bridge a projected $181 million shortfall. Management and Budget Executive Director Daniel Ramos presented the Fiscal Year 2027 proposal to the Harris County Commissioners Court on Monday, with a plan to cover the shortfall with cost savings, land sales, and other new revenues -- and by adopting the Voter-Approval Rate (VAR), the maximum rate increase allowed under Texas law without voter approval. Should commissioners approve the VAR next month, the overall property tax rate -- which includes the Harris County Flood Control District, the Harris Health hospital district, the Port of Houston, and the county's general fund -- will increase from $0.6241 to about $0.68 per $100 of appraised value. Commissioners Adrian Garcia (D-Pct. 2) and Lesley Briones (D-Pct. 4) blamed the county's budget woes on unfunded mandates from the state, Texas lawmakers' refusal to expand Medicaid, and federal changes to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program and the Affordable Care Act. () " Can Austin break the costly cycle of homelessness, jail and crisis? A new program aims to do that." via - About six months behind bars, Marcus Martin walked out of the Travis County Correctional Complex in Southeast Austin, a broad smile stretched across his face. He's been incarcerated before, but he believes this time is different. Outside the facility, several people awaited his release in their vehicles, blasting the air conditioning, while another went inside to greet Martin, made sure he had all of his belongings and walked him through what came next. The team waiting for him were not social workers, case managers or family, but sworn Austin Police Department officers assigned to a new program called No Wrong Door, a cross-agency effort aimed at helping people experiencing homelessness with complex mental health disorders who have frequent interactions with law enforcement and public health systems. Martin is one of roughly 950 people local officials identify as the county's highest "utilizers," residents whose repeated arrests, emergency room visits, psychiatric crises and criminal trespasses cost an estimated $137 million in public resources each year while often leaving the underlying problems untreated. Austin leaders believe No Wrong Door, could change that by coordinating police, hospitals, homeless service providers and other agencies around people who have proven hardest for existing systems to reach. For Martin, a series of life events and a bad breakup led to him becoming homeless for several years. Drug use kept him there and away from his family. "With me going down the rabbit hole I was going down, it wasn't productive or beneficial for me to be around them," he said. "I was being selfish, to be honest with you, and chose drugs over my own safety." That rabbit hole led to frequent interactions with local law enforcement and, eventually, a jail sentence. It also led to Martin being identified as a candidate for No Wrong Door while behind bars. Officers in the program met with him while he was incarcerated to determine what support he would need upon release to stay healthy and out of jail. For Martin, that meant checking in at an Integral Care clinic to continue receiving mental health treatment. Martin said "I'm ready to grow," he said. "I think it's gonna be a beautiful thing." () " Bexar County health department at risk as ARPA money runs out" via Josh Archote - Two years into the COVID-19 pandemic, Bexar County spent millions in federal pandemic relief dollars on public health programs -- with the goal of getting more involved in preventative health, preparing for future pandemics and addressing longstanding health inequities. Now, the funds are expiring at the same time the county budget is being squeezed, raising uncertainty about the future of the county's public health department, particularly its newly created Preventative Health Division. Created in 2022, the division now operates a $10 million annual budget, including 28 staff positions and programs supporting victims of domestic violence, elder abuse and other public health initiatives, according to a county budget document. Given the budget picture, some county commissioners are suggesting combining county efforts with University Health's Public Health Division, which was also established that year with the help of temporary American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding. Former Bexar County Judge Nelson Wolff , who championed the project, said in an interview that he wasn't sure if the county's preventative health campaigns had been effective -- or what the division had done since he left office. "I don't know whether they've done any good with it or not," he said. "Maybe just another bureaucratic department, as far as I know, and if that's true, then there's no need to have it. But if they have done some good things and they can be transferred over to University Hospital, then that ought to be done." () " McKinney voters move to recall mayor, council members following approval of mosque" via ' Sarah Bahari - A group of McKinney residents has launched an effort to recall the mayor and three city council members, a week after the city council unanimously approved a contentious proposal for a new mosque. Organizers cited a "loss of public confidence" in the ability of the elected officials to represent the city's residents in filings submitted this week to the city. The recall effort seeks to remove from office Mayor Bill Cox and council members Justin Beller , Ger e Feltus, and Ernest Lynch. In a statement, the mayor said residents have "every right to make their voices heard and to participate in the processes available to them." "Upholding the law and the constitutional principles that guide our government is a fundamental responsibility," he said. "Our focus remains on serving the people of McKinney and continuing the important work before us." () BUSINESS NEWS " Amazon confirms Dog's Head robotics facility, plans up to 500 new jobs in Austin" via Travis Webb - A map shows the roughly 2,650-acre Dog's Head development site in Southeast Austin, where Amazon said Thursday it plans to build an advanced robotics manufacturing facility. Amazon has confirmed plans to build a multibillion-dollar robotics manufacturing facility at Dog's Head in Southeast Austin. The facility is expected to create as many as 500 manufacturing and engineering jobs and will produce the robotics systems used across the online retail giant's operations to handle repetitive tasks and heavy lifting, Amazon said Thursday . Mayor Kirk Watson said Amazon did not seek economic incentives or public money for its facility, echoing comments he made during the city's approval of the Dog's Head financing plan. () " Elon Musk's Starbase wants to expand in south Texas" via Reynaldo Lea ños Jr. - On a scorching August afternoon in south Texas, Bekah Hinojosa, the co-founder of the South Texas Environmental Justice Center, blasts the A/C in her car. As she drives down Highway 4 towards Boca Chica Beach, large 18-wheelers and silver glistening Cybertrucks zoom past her on the opposite lane. "This road is always under construction," said Hinojosa. "SpaceX is rapidly colonizing and changing the entire landscape of Boca Chica." Very soon the newly created city of Starbase, and Elon Musk 's SpaceX, could change this area by the Gulf of Mexico, even more. This city was established in 2025 and is now asking its residents to consider annexing around 7,100 acres of surrounding land, including state and private property. The city was created, in part, as a way to help grow its SpaceX workforce and increase its capacity for developing, and the manufacturing needed for more rocket launches. In April of 2025 the Federal Aviation Administration approved SpaceX's request to increase launches from its Boca Chica Launch Site. These operations include, "up to 25 annual Starship/Super Heavy orbital launches, up to 25 annual landings of Starship, up to 25 annual landings of Super Heavy, and vehicle upgrades," according to the FAA document. **" Data centers in Texas prove a key topic months away from midterm elections"** via [CBS News](https://substack.com/redirect/7a328340-8051-4088-907c-afaf570f2014?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)' **Steven Rosenbaum** - As the public backlash to data center construction continues in both suburban and rural parts of Texas, Gov. **Greg Abbott** is touting that major tech companies like Google, Amazon and Microsoft are signing on to guidelines he has implemented to "ensure data center development does not come at the expense of Texas families or communities".

The guidelines include undergoing audits from ERCOT and the Public Utility Commission of Texas over electricity use, water consumption, noise and light pollution and other impacts on nearby property owners. Abbott says data center projects that do not comply with the audits will not be approved.

A recent poll by Texas Public Opinion Research shows more than 75 percent of Texans support requiring large AI data centers to disclose water consumption, avoid tapping overused aquifers, fund conservation projects, fund their own grid upgrades, and not pass the costs onto other electricity ratepayers. _([CBS News](https://substack.com/redirect/7a328340-8051-4088-907c-afaf570f2014?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Texas Lacks Statewide Record of Water Use, Local Tax Breaks for Data Centers"** via [The Texan](https://substack.com/redirect/5c34bfed-c4a7-4799-9df0-6ef27c127f98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Isaiah Mitchell** - The Texas Legislature is preparing to address data center development using information reported by the developers themselves, according to state officials.

During a lengthy hearing in the Texas Capitol on Wednesday, several public officials told the State Affairs Committee of the Texas House that agencies do not comprehensively track data centers ' water usage or the local tax breaks they receive. The state instead relies on survey responses.

The committee heard from **Pablo Vegas** , CEO of the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT), and **Thomas Gleeson** , chairman of the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUC), the two agencies responsible for managing Texas' electrical infrastructure. Earlier this month, Gov. **Greg Abbott** asked these agencies to audit all data center projects in the process of connecting to the Texas power grid, specifying that the PUC and ERCOT must learn which projects benefit from state and local tax breaks.

"Are either the PUC or ERCOT set up to undertake that type of review of local tax incentives or abatements, or anything on the state level, for that matter?" state Rep. **Chris Turner** (D-Arlington) asked Pablo Vegas and Thomas Gleeson. Vegas told Turner that they'll ask for this information through a survey.
